meta.titre: Methods of Cooking Food: Choosing, Comparing and Saving Fuel
meta.sous_theme: Moist, dry and fat methods, and fuel economy

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Food and Nutrition past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: On a Saturday in Douala a family cooks rice, a pot of stew and fried plantain for lunch, and the cylinder of cooking gas must last the whole month. The choice of method decides how soft, tasty, safe and nutritious the meal is, and also how much fuel it uses. This is why the GCE asks you to name methods, compare their advantages and disadvantages and give ways of saving fuel in the home.

items: Heat is needed to cook food; fuels such as gas, charcoal, wood and electricity supply it.
Vitamins B and C dissolve in water and are easily lost.
Fat is a source of energy, and fried food contains more fat.

sections.titre: The main cooking methods and how to choose between them
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Why we cook food
Cooking makes food safe (it kills most harmful bacteria), easier to chew and digest, more pleasant in taste, smell and appearance, and helps it to keep longer. It can also destroy some vitamins, so the method must be chosen with care.

### The main methods

| Group | Method | How it works | Examples |
|---|---|---|---|
| Moist heat | Boiling | food in water bubbling vigorously at about 100 °C | rice, yams, eggs |
| | Simmering | food in liquid heated to just below boiling, bubbles barely break the surface | soups, tough meat |
| | Steaming | food cooked by steam from boiling water, not touching the water | fish, vegetables, steamed puddings |
| | Stewing | small pieces cooked slowly in a little liquid in a covered pan, liquid eaten with the food | meat, vegetable stews |
| | Poaching | gentle cooking in liquid below boiling | eggs, fish |
| Dry heat | Baking | hot air in an oven | bread, cakes |
| | Roasting | oven heat with fat, or over an open fire | chicken, plantain |
| | Grilling | heat from above or below, fast | fish, meat, toast |
| Fat | Shallow frying | a little fat in a pan | eggs, fish |
| | Deep frying | enough hot fat to cover the food | chips, doughnuts |

**Blanching** is plunging vegetables into boiling water for a short time and then cooling them quickly in cold water. It stops enzyme action, fixes colour and prepares food for freezing.

### Choosing a method
Use gentle moist heat (stewing, steaming) for tough foods and to keep nutrients; use dry heat for a brown, crisp surface; fried food is high in energy because it absorbs fat. In a moist method the water-soluble vitamins (B and C) and minerals pass into the water, so use that water in soup or sauce.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked to outline, state or compare the merits and drawbacks of a single method.
variantes.contenu_markdown:
Boiling is a frequent question.
**Advantages:** 1. it is simple and needs no special equipment; 2. it needs no added fat; 3. it softens hard foods such as dried beans and tough roots; 4. several foods can be cooked together in one pot; 5. the liquid can be kept and used for soup; 6. a large amount can be cooked at once.
**Disadvantages:** 1. water-soluble vitamins (B and C) and minerals are lost into the water; 2. the food can become too soft and lose its flavour and colour; 3. it gives no brown or crisp surface; 4. tough foods take long, which uses much fuel; 5. food can be overcooked if forgotten.
Give the number asked, no more.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked for ways to save gas, charcoal or electricity in the home.

sections.enonce_markdown: Give three benefits and two drawbacks of cooking food by steaming. (5 marks)

etapes.action: Analyse the command word and the numbers.
etapes.justification: The question asks for main points in a few words. The numbers 3 and 2 give 5 marks, so each point earns one mark and the answer must have two headed lists (benefits and drawbacks).
etapes.resultat_markdown: Write 3 advantages and 2 disadvantages, nothing more.

etapes.justification: Food sits above boiling water and is cooked by the steam, so it never touches the water.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Vitamins and minerals cannot dissolve in water; no fat is needed.

etapes.justification: Choose ideas that are not repeats: nutrients, fat, and digestibility or shape.
etapes.resultat_markdown: 1. Few vitamins and minerals are lost. 2. No fat is added. 3. The food keeps its shape, colour and flavour and is easy to digest.

etapes.justification: Think of time and equipment, which are the real drawbacks.
etapes.resultat_markdown: 1. It takes longer than boiling for many foods. 2. A steamer or covered pot with a rack is needed, and the water must not boil dry.

sections.conclusion_markdown: **Advantages of steaming:** 1. few vitamins and minerals are lost; 2. no fat is added; 3. food keeps its shape, colour and flavour and is easy to digest. **Disadvantages:** 1. it is slow, so it uses fuel for a long time; 2. it needs a steamer or other special arrangement and the water must not boil dry.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing that boiling keeps all the vitamins in the food.
items.pourquoi_faux: Vitamins B and C and some minerals dissolve in the cooking water, and heat destroys part of vitamin C, so boiling causes losses.
items.correction_markdown: Say that boiling loses water-soluble vitamins and minerals unless the cooking water is used in soup or sauce.

items.erreur_markdown: Treating simmering and boiling as the same thing.
items.pourquoi_faux: In boiling the liquid bubbles vigorously. In simmering it is just below boiling, with small bubbles that barely break the surface, and it is gentler on tough food.
items.correction_markdown: Simmer soups and tough meat; boil water for rice or yams.

items.erreur_markdown: Saying that frying is a dry method that uses no fat.
items.pourquoi_faux: Frying needs fat or oil (a little for shallow frying, enough to cover for deep frying) and so adds energy to the food.
items.correction_markdown: Frying is a fat method. Baking, roasting and grilling are the dry-heat methods.

items.erreur_markdown: Answering a fuel-saving question with: use less gas, avoid wasting gas, cook with care.
items.pourquoi_faux: These repeat the question and give no practical action, so the examiner awards no marks.
items.correction_markdown: Give actions: cover pans, turn the flame down once boiling, soak beans, use a pressure cooker, match the pan to the burner.

items.enonce_markdown: Name the cooking method described in each case: (a) a cake cooked by hot air in an oven; (b) fish cooked under a hot grill element; (c) fish cooked by steam above boiling water; (d) doughnuts cooked in enough hot oil to cover them; (e) tough meat cooked slowly in a little liquid in a covered pan.

A family buys a cylinder of cooking gas for $6\,000$ FCFA that lasts 24 days. After covering pans, soaking beans before cooking and turning the flame down once the food boils, one cylinder lasts 30 days. (a) Find the cost per day before and after. (b) Find the saving over 30 days. (c) State two other ways of saving gas.
items.solution_markdown: (a) Before: $6\,000 \div 24 = 250$, so **250 FCFA per day**. After: $6\,000 \div 30 = 200$, so **200 FCFA per day**. (b) Over 30 days the old habits use $250 \times 30 = 7\,500$ FCFA of gas and the new habits use $6\,000$ FCFA, so the saving is $7\,500 - 6\,000 =$ **$1\,500$ FCFA**. (c) Any two of: use a pressure cooker for long-cooking foods; match the pan to the burner; cook foods together in one pot; thaw frozen food first; keep burners clean and check for leaks.

items.enonce_markdown: (a) Explain why green beans are blanched before being frozen. (b) Why are they cooled quickly in cold water afterwards? (c) Name the best method for a tough piece of meat and give a reason. (d) State two ways in which cooking improves food.
items.solution_markdown: (a) Blanching in boiling water for a short time stops the enzymes that would otherwise spoil the colour, flavour and texture of the beans during frozen storage, so the beans stay green and fresh. (b) Cooling stops the cooking at once, so the beans do not become soft and lose vitamins. (c) **Stewing** (or simmering): slow cooking in a little liquid softens the tough fibres, and the liquid is eaten with the meat so nothing is lost. (d) Any two of: kills harmful bacteria; makes the food softer and easier to digest; improves taste, smell and look; helps it to keep longer.

items_markdown: Moist methods: boiling, simmering, steaming, stewing, poaching. Dry methods: baking, roasting, grilling. Fat methods: shallow and deep frying.
Boiling loses water-soluble vitamins and minerals into the water; steaming and stewing lose less.
Blanching is a short plunge in boiling water followed by quick cooling; it is done before freezing vegetables.
To save gas: use lids, match pan to burner, simmer after boiling, soak beans, use a pressure cooker, cook foods together, thaw first.
Answer advantage and disadvantage questions in two headed lists with the exact number of points asked.
